institutionName: UiT The Arctic University of Norway

questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The location. For me, the most important was going to a place with beautiful nature. But also going to af city with af nice student environment.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It's is not a cliché that exchange will be one of the most amazing experiences of your life:) You really learn something about yourself.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Sometimes a bit confusing, but it was doable.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was an introduction week at the university, which was very nice and helpful.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
It is generally very hard to find housing in Tromsø, and it is quite expensive.
I recommend applying for housing very early on through Samskipnaden.
If you want to live privately, finding someone else so that you can share a flat/house might be easier. But I have friends that managed to find a spot in different norwegian collectives.
Look at
hybel.no
or make a post in one of the different Facebook-groups for people renting out og looking for places to live. Leie / hybel i Tromsø.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer:
You can maybe find a better location than then student dorms. Student dorms are not neccesarily as social as we are used to in Denmark, so be aware of that. And there is a lot of exchange in the dorms since quite a lot of the students will be international. Therefore it might be nicer in a collective/shared flat.
Private housing can be quite demanding and expensive though. And you might have to deal with some unprofessional landlords...

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: You should be aware that if you are a Danish student, you should apply for the student dorms through samskipnaden very early on!

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
Very annoying that they don't write anywhere in the course catalogue that you can take more courses than are present in the catalogue, if you are Danish! 
Find the courses on UiT's website, where you can see all the courses, also taught in norwegian. Even though they are not on the official list of courses offered to exchange students, you can apply for them as well!

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You just had to fill out a formular

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Not that much. The Exchange coordinator at UiT is not that good. But you can find your faculty/institute leader or something like that and they are very helpful!

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer:
I wanted to take some very interesting master courses, but unfortunately, thats is no longer allowed at UiT if you are a bachelors student...
However, of the bachelor-courses that I applied for, I got all the courses I wanted, and even managed to change later on, when I discovered a Norwegian course that i would rather have.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Find your institute leader and text them if you have questions about joining a specific course. They will help you.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: They were nice, but the academic level is quite a lot lower than in Copenhagen. However they also have some super cool courses, and courses where a lot of teachers have put a lot of effort into making it a cool course.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Way easier than in Copenhagen and way less expectations at the exam.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
Mainly lectures, very few theoretical exercise classes, if any, which is quite a shame. Laboratory exercises though.
However, theres only very few at the lectures, so there's opportunities to ask the lecturer.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
BIO-1103 Botanikk
BIO-2504 Fish physiology
BIO-2009 Nordlige biologiske ressurser (eller evt. Biologiske ressurser i nord) Det er det samme.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Nordlige biologiske ressourcer!
Det er et lidt skørt fag, men man kommer på en fantastisk ekskursion til Alta og får lov at prøve nogle ret særlige ting og kommer på et kortere marint togt på et forskningsskib.
Det handler om norsk forvaltning af naturen, og man lærer en masse om hvordan norge forholder sig til naturen og hvilke ressurser der er. Et veldig bra kurs!

Botanikk er lige som Organismers Diversitet på KU biologi bachelor ift. alger og planter. Bare mindre dybdegående... Så ikke om arktiske planter, men dejligt at have et fag man lidt havde haft i forvejen.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer:
Food is expensive...
And if you like being outdoors you might end up buying a lot of nice outdoor equipment;)
Problems with landlord...

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Food was more expensive. Beers extremely expensive.
Public transportation was very cheap if you bought the monthly pass for young adults on Svipper. And the Tromsø zone is very big so you can go really far without having to buy extra.
And very cheap to go on trips - become member of DNT and you can book beds in lovely huts for nearly no money!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
A lot!
Choir, a lot of sports, Waffle-friday... Gardening, knitting...

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
The Choir was very nice - and a lovely way to meet both locals and other exchange students.
TSI - the student sports association. Theres a lot of different sports activities.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Go as much as you can to the mountains! Kvaløya, Senja, Sommarøy. Go to the Lyngen Alps!!!
The DNT-hut system is an amazing way to explore the nature if you are not to much into camping in a tent.
Go climbing and swimming.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy! Helps a lot being Danish and able to understand Norwegian.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join events and actively engage with them. They might not come and talk to you by themselves.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: They eat dinner very early, so all social arrangement starts when you would normally have dinner...

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The respect and use of the nature

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
- You will never regret going on a trip to the fjell!
- Don't be afraid to ask other people if they want to join you doing something; they are just like you looking for someone to hang out with!
- Be active! Don't wait for others to ask you, but do the things you want to do! Be the one that plans the trip, and reach out for others.

- Don't be to disappointed with your courses; they might not be as you had hoped, but see it as an opportunity to go and enjoy Northen Norway even more!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Get a Norwegian phone number and a TURBO (BUA) account! Then you can rent outdoor-equipment for free! Tents, sleeping bags, skiis, snowshoes...
Bring your hiking boots! And a good backpack, sleeping bag and mat if you want to go camping a lot. It is annoying to coordinate going to turbo all the time.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Experiencing how you can live and shape your life in a completely different way than you are used to! You get so many new hobbys and friends instantly that you might never want to leave again.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: It is quite demanding that theres is always so much to do and you feel like you have to make the most out of everything. So remember that it is okay to say no and have a chill day at home, even though the sun is shining:)

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer:
Tromsø is extreme, yes, but in an amazing way.
Don't fear the darkness and the cold, you will have such an amazing time skiing and watching the everlasting sunset and northern lights that you won't notice.
However, if I had not loved being active, hiking and in the mountains, Tromsø is a small city and you might be bored after some months. For me, the mountains compensated for everything bad, but it might be different for you:)

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
